project_overview: This Vue.js application appears to be a web portal related to examinations and course selections. The project utilizes a series of Vue components, likely managed within a single application instance, navigating users through various stages of registration, result viewing, and course exploration. The dependency graph indicates a primary flow driven by route navigation within the components, suggesting a user interface focused on guided workflows. This architecture relies heavily on Vue components for rendering and managing user interactions.

macro_trends.title: High-Level Component Dependency Risks
macro_trends.description: Several Vue components, particularly those within the UI layer (e.g., ResultPage.vue, ApplicationServices.vue), appear to be heavily reliant on other components for route navigation, potentially introducing fragility and increasing the impact of changes within these core components. Circular dependencies are not immediately obvious, but the network of connections warrants closer scrutiny.

macro_trends.title: Potential Centralized Component Fragility
macro_trends.description: The high concentration of components directly connected to ResultPage.vue suggests a potential centralization point for critical application logic. Modifications or issues within ResultPage.vue could have far-reaching consequences.

key_workflows.name: Examination Registration & Result Flow
key_workflows.description: This workflow starts with the user navigating through components like ExamFormSubmission and FeeDetails, potentially converging on ResultPage.vue to view their examination results. The flow is facilitated by router navigation between components, showing a clear user journey.

key_workflows.name: Course Exploration & Selection
key_workflows.description: The 'iLike' components and their related views represent a core workflow for users to explore and select courses.  The route navigation between these components highlights a key user interaction pattern within the application.
